newsitem.title: UK: Unilever sees chemical sale erasing debt.
newsitem.headline: Unilever sees chemical sale erasing debt.

text.p: Niall FitzGerald, chairman of Anglo-Dutch foods and consumer products group Unilever NV/Plc, said on Tuesday the planned sale of its speciality chemicals business would remove net borrowings from the balance sheet in the short term.
"The cash received from the sale would remove net borrowings from the balance sheet in the short-term," he told a news conference.
Earlier Unilever said it planned to sell the business, which analysts expect to fetch between 4.5 and 5.0 billion stg.

The company's net debt stands at about 1.7 billion stg, and the disposal proceeds are expected to free up sizeable resources to expand the business in, possibly through major acquisition, FitzGerald added.
He told reporters at a presentation following the release of the company's annual results that the best route for the disposal was most likely to be via a trade sale.
"We have a carefully-defined list of what we may do with (the proceeds), which I am not prepared to discuss," he added.
Unilever has said its current priority product categories are tea, ice cream, yellow fats, detergents, personal wash, mask skins and fragrance.
FitzGerald said the company would seek to invest "where we are getting growth".
The group's businesses in the emerging and developing markets of Asia, Latin America and Eastern Europe performed very strongly in 1996, it noted.
"In China I would like to have a business ten times the size," the chairman added.
